JINDABYNE, NSW, AUSTRALIA · 30 June 2026

feelzlike, the daily decision app for travellers staying near snow, now spans ten regions across australia, japan and new zealand.

The town-first weather, road and mountain-comparison app for off-mountain visitors has grown from three launch regions to ten across three countries, and now ships live powder, wind and road alerts, a multi-day trip planner and a premium tier.

feelzlike, the progressive web app purpose-built for travellers based in resort towns rather than on the mountain, now serves ten live regions across Australia, Japan and New Zealand. The app is available now at feelzlike.com and installs directly to mobile home screens with no app-store download required.

feelzlike is built around a single morning question that every off-mountain visitor asks themselves: which mountain do I drive to today? The app answers that question by combining live weather, official road status, snow conditions and a fair side-by-side comparison of every resort the visitor's town serves · all anchored to the town the visitor is actually staying in.

Where feelzlike is now

  • Ten regions across three countries. Australia: the Snowy Mountains, Victoria's High Country and Tasmania. Japan: Yamanouchi, Nozawa Onsen and Iiyama in Nagano. New Zealand: Queenstown, Wanaka, Mt Hutt and Ruapehu.
  • The towns visitors actually stay in. From Jindabyne, Bright and Cooma to Yudanaka, Nozawa Onsen, Queenstown, Wanaka, Methven and Ohakune · more than twenty base towns and the resorts they serve.
  • The mountains people drive to. Thredbo, Perisher, Selwyn and Charlotte Pass; Mt Buller, Falls Creek and Mt Hotham; the eighteen interconnected fields of Shiga Kogen, plus Nozawa Onsen and Madarao; Coronet Peak, The Remarkables, Cardrona, Treble Cone, Mt Hutt, Whakapapa and Turoa.
  • Live data, not stale screenshots. Continuous integration with official sources including the Bureau of Meteorology, NSW LiveTraffic, VicEmergency and the Japan Meteorological Agency, plus Open-Meteo and region-aware weather radar.
  • Curated stays and eats. Hundreds of hand-checked venues across the base towns, with country-aware filters covering ryokan onsen and tattoo policies in Japan and drying-rooms and ski-storage in Australia and New Zealand.
  • A daily personalised call. An optional thirty-second profile tailors the mountain ranking to the visitor's skill level, discipline, priorities and risk tolerance.

What is new since launch

  • Powder, wind and road alerts. Visitors can follow a town and be told when fresh snow, wind holds or road closures are likely · across all ten regions.
  • A multi-day trip planner. Stack the next seven days across every mountain a town serves and read the week at a glance.
  • Favourite towns. Save up to three towns so the app opens straight into the one you are staying in.
  • A fortnightly newsletter. An opt-in digest of conditions and the season's signal, with double opt-in confirmation.
  • A premium tier. The alerting and planning tools, free for every visitor through the launch period.

Why town-first matters

Every existing snow app starts with the mountain. feelzlike starts with the town · because that is where the off-mountain visitor wakes up. The audience the app serves is the family in a Jindabyne lodge with a non-skiing partner, the couple in a Yudanaka ryokan with three resorts within forty minutes, the Queenstown apartment weighing Coronet Peak against The Remarkables, the Bright pub patron weighing Hotham against Falls Creek over breakfast. On-mountain lodging in these regions is two to four times the price of in-town accommodation and supply has not recovered to demand since the pandemic · the off-mountain stay is now the norm, and feelzlike is built for it.

feelzlike does not tell you which mountain is best. That call is yours. What it does is put every number you need, from every official source, on one screen · in the language of the town you woke up in · in under thirty seconds. The feelzlike product team

Until 31 December 2026 every feelzlike feature, including powder alerts and the trip planner, is free with no credit card required. From 1 January 2027 the alerting and planning tools move to a subscription, while the core town weather, snow radar and side-by-side mountain comparison stay free for everyone.

Availability

feelzlike is a progressive web app. It works in every modern mobile browser and installs to the home screen with one tap on iOS and Android. There is nothing to download from the App Store or Google Play. The app is in English throughout, and bilingual in English and Japanese across the Japan regions of Yamanouchi, Nozawa Onsen and Iiyama.

About feelzlike

feelzlike is the daily decision app for people staying in resort towns near snow. Built on a town-first information architecture, the platform pairs live weather, road status and snow data with curated stays, eats and explore content for every base town it covers. feelzlike serves ten live regions across Australia, Japan and New Zealand and is structured to expand to Hokkaido, Hakuba, the European Alps and North America on the same town-first shape.
